recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to diagnosticReport-focus should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack; future core changes should use the later DiagnosticReport.procedure and supportingInfo decisions rather than reintroducing Procedure as a subject.
issue_request: FHIR-32575 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It requested removing Procedure from DiagnosticReport.subject and adding a focus extension, 0..* Reference(Any), for non-subject focal components such as a Procedure or manufacturing process evaluated by a quality report.
initial_application: HL7/fhir PR #2598 applied the issue for R5. Commit 9622124f4e removed Procedure from DiagnosticReport.subject, and merge 8b80ac4b98 brought in the subject removal plus the DiagnosticReport focus extension work.
additional_context: OO minutes show the January 2023 discussion reopened an initial not-persuasive motion to confirm the BR&R manufacturing-process use case, then the January 26 main call accepted the block vote 10-0-2. Later R6 issues FHIR-49614 and FHIR-50866 added and clarified DiagnosticReport.procedure for performed procedures reported on by the DiagnosticReport, and FHIR-45132 expanded DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo.reference. The original diagnosticReport-focus extension is now authored in the FHIR Extension Pack with canonical URL http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/diagnosticReport-focus.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active core DiagnosticReport source already satisfies the subject cleanup and current core modeling, while the remaining focus-extension artifact is maintained outside this core checkout.

related_jiras.note: Added DiagnosticReport.procedure 0..* Reference(Procedure), giving current core an explicit element for performed procedures that are reported on.
Kept DiagnosticReport.procedure rather than replacing it with partOf and clarified it as the performed procedure.
Expanded DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo.reference, showing later DiagnosticReport work around additional focal/supporting references.
